circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit is a 5. 281-kilometer track located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, designed by Hermann Tilke, which has served as the venue for Formula One's season-concluding Abu Dhabi Grand Prix since 2009. The circuit represents the second of four Middle Eastern Formula One venues, following Bahrain's establishment and preceding those in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street track encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix alongside various support series competitions. Designated with an FIA Grade 1 licence, the venue serves as a premier motorsport facility for multiple racing categories.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Styria, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit in Spielberg originally opened as the Österreichring and accommodated the Austrian Grand Prix continuously between 1970 and 1987. Following a redesign and shortening, the track was renamed and reintroduced as a Grand Prix venue from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: Baku City Circuit is a street racing venue in Azerbaijan's capital, featuring a 6. 003 km layout that ranks as the fourth-longest track in Formula One. The circuit first hosted the European Grand Prix in 2016, before becoming the permanent home of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix from 2017 onwards.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km track that hosted the Middle East's inaugural Formula One Grand Prix that year. The venue features multiple configurations and holds FIA Grade 1 status, accommodating various motorsport categories including GP2 racing and endurance events alongside its annual Formula One championship race.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: The Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers near Barcelona in northeastern Spain and features a balanced layout combining extended straights with diverse corner types, making it versatile for testing various driving skills. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: Spa-Francorchamps is a 7. 004 km Belgian racing circuit situated near the town of Spa in the Walloon region, which has served as the venue for the Formula One Belgian Grand Prix since 1950. The track has maintained continuous Grand Prix hosting since 1985, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island near Montreal, this 4. 361-kilometre track serves as the home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond its Formula One heritage, the circuit has accommodated various international racing series including sports cars, open-wheel competitions, and stock car events.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, this Chinese motorsport facility is primarily renowned for hosting the Chinese Grand Prix, which took place annually from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. The venue has expanded its racing calendar to include the Shanghai ePrix championship beginning in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone Circuit, located in England near Northamptonshire, has been synonymous with British motorsport since hosting the inaugural 1948 British Grand Prix and the first-ever Formula One World Championship race two years later. The venue served as a rotating host for the British Grand Prix alongside Aintree and Brands Hatch until becoming its permanent home in 1987, and continues to welcome international racing series including MotoGP.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, a 4. 381 km circuit located near Budapest in Hungary, hosted the first Formula One Grand Prix held within the Eastern Bloc when it opened in 1986. Built in just eight months following an October 1985 start date, the track was constructed outside the city after government preference overrode plans for a street circuit in Budapest's central park.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, the Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km track constructed in 1922, making it mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built racing circuit. The venue hosts the Italian Grand Prix annually since 1949, earning its nickname "the Temple of Speed" for its distinctive fast straights and high-speed configuration.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: The Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807-kilometre Japanese motorsport facility situated in Mie Prefecture and operated by Honda's Mobilityland division. With a capacity of 155,000 spectators, it serves as a premier venue for Formula One and Super Formula racing championships.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that weaves through Paradise, Nevada, incorporating sections of Las Vegas Boulevard lined with the city's premier hotels and entertainment venues. The layout features several of Las Vegas's iconic landmarks, such as MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas, as part of its racing route.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: The 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez in Mexico City is named after two Mexican racing brothers who died in separate incidents during the 1960s and early 1970s. The venue has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix since 2015 on its current configuration, having previously held the race on a different layout through 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary street circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, Florida, measuring 3. 363 miles with 19 corners and an average qualifying speed near 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design specifically for Formula One racing, the track became home to the Miami Grand Prix when it joined the championship calendar in 2022.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street track that winds through the urban streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine, following the coastline around Monaco's harbour. Though officially named after the principality, it is widely known by the Monte Carlo designation due to the circuit's location predominantly within that district.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the coastal dunes near Amsterdam, the 4. 259 km Zandvoort circuit in the Netherlands rejoined Formula One in 2021 to host the Dutch Grand Prix after a lengthy absence. The track will conclude its current F1 partnership at the end of 2026.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is situated north of Doha in Qatar and spans 5. 419 kilometers with a prominent 1. 068-kilometer main straight.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian racing circuit in São Paulo that opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate the late Formula 1 driver José Carlos Pace. The track operates in a counterclockwise direction and serves as the venue for Brazil's Formula 1 Grand Prix, while also featuring a separate kart facility honoring another legendary Brazilian racing driver.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street track situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coastline that has hosted the Formula One Saudi Arabian Grand Prix annually since its debut in 2021.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through downtown Singapore and the Kallang district, utilizing public roads around the Marina Bay waterfront for its racing layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located near Barcelona in Catalonia, this 4. 657 km Spanish racing venue features a balanced design combining extended straights with diverse corner complexes, making it suitable for testing multiple aspects of vehicle performance. The facility, which holds FIA Grade 1 certification, accommodates up to 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 facility that serves as the permanent home of Formula One's United States Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the track hosts multiple racing series including MotoGP's Motorcycle Grand Prix of the Americas and the Lone Star Le Mans endurance event, alongside various other motorsport categories past and present.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a British-Thai racing driver currently competing for Williams in Formula One under the Thai flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Fernando Alonso is a Spanish driver currently racing for Aston Martin in Formula One, having claimed two world championships during his tenure with Renault in 2005 and 2006 alongside 32 Grand Prix victories. Beyond the pinnacle of motorsport, Alonso has achieved significant success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans 24 Hours victories and the 2018-19 FIA World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to have won both the F1 drivers' title and the world endurance championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, having secured six victories following his entry to the series in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British motorsport competitor currently racing in Formula One with the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently races in Formula One for the Audi team, bringing his competitive spirit to the sport's premier championship.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from a 13-season career that has yielded 10 Grand Prix victories. He achieved two runner-up finishes in the World Drivers' Championship during consecutive years with Mercedes, in 2019 and 2020.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto, an Argentine racing driver, currently competes in Formula One for the Alpine team.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian driver, races in the European Le Mans Series' LMP2 category while holding a reserve driver position with Haas in Formula One. He has made seven Formula One starts between 2024 and 2025.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly, a French driver currently racing for Alpine, previously secured a Formula One victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while driving for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: French-Algerian driver Isack Alexandre Hadjar races for Red Bull Racing under the French flag in Formula One.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Ferrari, holding a record seven world championship titles that he shares with Michael Schumacher. He also leads the sport in multiple statistical categories, including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes throughout his career.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One after establishing himself as a competitive midfield competitor over multiple seasons. Beyond his single-seater commitments, he achieved significant success in endurance racing, notably securing victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand-born racing driver currently competing in Formula One with the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a driver from Monaco, races for Ferrari in Formula One and has achieved nine race victories throughout his nine seasons in the sport. He came closest to winning the drivers' championship in 2022, finishing as runner-up that year while competing for the Scuderia.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish racing driver currently competing in the FIA World Endurance Championship with WRT as a BMW factory driver, while also participating in NASCAR's Cup Series with Trackhouse Racing. The driver previously spent time in Formula One across two separate stints, racing from 2014 to 2020 and again from 2022 to 2024.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver, secured the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship while racing for McLaren. Over his eight-season career, he has accumulated 12 Grand Prix victories and continues to compete for the same team.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. The driver achieved a career milestone by securing victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while competing for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez competes for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing extensive experience from 15 seasons in the sport. He finished second in the 2023 drivers' championship while driving for Red Bull and has claimed six Grand Prix victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri currently races for McLaren in Formula One, where he has secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his four seasons in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Australian driver Daniel Ricciardo, known by his "Honey Badger" moniker, participated in Formula One racing over a 14-season span from 2011 through 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his career in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, having accumulated seven Grand Prix victories throughout his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes for Williams in Formula One, having secured four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver currently racing in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition. He previously competed in Formula One during the 2023 and 2024 seasons before transitioning to endurance racing.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently competing for Aston Martin in the sport's premier racing series.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda is a Japanese driver who held a Formula One seat from 2021 through 2025 and currently works as a reserve driver for Red Bull Racing and its sister team Racing Bulls.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: The Dutch-Belgian driver competes for Red Bull Racing and has claimed four consecutive world championships between 2021 and 2024. Across 12 seasons in the sport, he has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu holds the distinction of being the sole Chinese competitor in Formula One's history, having raced in the sport between 2022 and 2024. He currently operates as a reserve driver for Cadillac's Formula One team.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Alpine Racing competes as Renault's works team from its Enstone base, having rebranded under the Alpine sports car nameplate in 2021 after operating as Renault F1 Team. The squad secured its only victory in the current era when Esteban Ocon triumphed at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix, and continues to use Mercedes power units.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, the British automotive manufacturer, has maintained a presence in Formula One through different organizational structures, with the current iteration operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari, the racing arm of the Italian automotive manufacturer Ferrari, stands as Formula One's longest-running and most accomplished competitor, never missing a World Championship season since 1950. The iconic team, nicknamed after their emblematic horse symbol, has remained a cornerstone of the sport throughout its entire modern history.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: Haas Formula is an American-licensed Formula One team founded by NASCAR team owner Gene Haas in 2014, competing from 2016 onwards. Leadership changed in early 2024 when Ayao Komatsu took over the team principal position from long-serving Guenther Steiner, who had led the operation since its establishment.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: A Swiss racing organisation established in 1970, Sauber developed into a Formula One constructor after joining the sport in 1993 and competed for over three decades. The team achieved notable success in endurance racing, including victory at Le Mans in 1989, before undergoing various transformations throughout its F1 tenure until ceasing operations in 2025. Audi acquired the operation and its assets in 2024 to establish the foundation for its own F1 programme.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing is a British Formula One outfit headquartered at its Woking facility, operating as a subsidiary within the broader McLaren Group structure under Bahraini ownership through Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has maintained a presence in Formula One since 1954 as both constructor and power unit supplier, with its current iteration based in Brackley and operating under a German licence. The team, now known as Mercedes-AMG Petronas, became jointly owned in 2022 by Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff in equal thirds. Mercedes-powered entries are traditionally associated with the "Silver Arrows" moniker.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that commenced competition in 2024, based in Faenza with an additional facility in Milton Keynes. As one of two Red Bull GmbH-owned constructors alongside Red Bull Racing, it operates as the energy drink company's second Formula One entry.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that debuted in 2024 as one of two teams owned by Red Bull GmbH, alongside Red Bull Racing. Operating from headquarters in Faenza with an additional facility in Milton Keynes, the team functions as a sister outfit within the Red Bull F1 structure.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, based in England but racing under an Austrian licence, has been a prominent Formula One team since its 2005 establishment as part of the Red Bull GmbH conglomerate. Christian Horner led the team for two decades until his 2025 departure, when Laurent Mekies assumed the leadership role. The outfit represents one of two Formula One entries owned by Red Bull, alongside Racing Bulls.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering stands as a British Formula One constructor founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, succeeding Williams's earlier failed racing venture. Currently competing as Atlassian Williams F1 Team, the operation is headquartered at its Grove, Oxfordshire facility and remains one of the sport's established teams.
